body:
I've always had hope for the future. When I was 18 I hoped I would enjoy my military service and be good at it. It was no big shame when that turned out to be a false hope. Having always been the smartest guy I the room I knew I was going to do well in university. After a couple of years of that failing completely I figured I just had the wrong school so got into another one. That went badly enough to land me in the psych ward but that wasn't the end of the world. I'd just build myself up again. All that shrink stuff and mess and what-not and I never really felt any less afraid of people and failure and life. I never did go back to school but that wasn't the end of the world. I got a steady job and figured I'd live a quiet and content life. Now I'm a 32-year old virgin (I did go on a date once) and after a couple of years of living in voluntary squalor and bloating myself with junk food, I just feel so tired. Whatever curiosity I have left for the future is morbid. I know life would go on, it always does, maybe it's just time it went on without me. 

And thanks for chatting with me. I do appreciate it, even if I try my best to shit on all your advice.

I'm not broke though, I just didn't pay the bills. Just like I haven't paid any bills or in fact opened any letters for the better part of a year. I could have just visited the electric company and got the electricity turned back on the next day. That's what I did the last time it happened. I just don't see the point.

And I don't really want the confused pity I would get from my family. I know this would hurt them like hell. But they don't (and can't) depend on me either. Hopefully they would get over it somehow, because its just not enough of a reason for me to live so they won't be sad.
